title: Contouring mitigates voiding at the lithium/ceramic electrolyte interface on discharging solid-state batteries - Nature Energy
gist: Oxford researchers (Bruce group) show that imprinting a 5 µm/30 µm egg-box topography on the Li/Li6PS5Cl interface raises the discharge current at which voiding starts tenfold (0.2 to 2 mA cm−2 at 2 MPa, 30 °C) for only ~5% volumetric energy-density cost. Contoured cells survive pulses up to 8–9 mA cm−2 and repeated WLTP EV drive cycles at 2 MPa and 60 °C where flat interfaces fail immediately, though contouring barely helps charge-side dendrites and scalable patterning (stamping, laser etching) remains unproven.

themes.theme: Discharge voiding as the binding constraint for lithium-metal solid-state batteries at practical pressure

insights.claim: In lithium-metal solid-state batteries, voids form at the Li/ceramic electrolyte interface during discharge when Li+ flux away from the interface through the electrolyte exceeds the rate at which Li can be transported to the interface within the anode, raising polarization and ultimately causing cell failure.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Discharge-rate capability, not just dendrites on charge, is a gating failure mode for solid-state EV cells.
insights.quote: Voiding occurs when the flux of Li+ away from the interface through the solid electrolyte exceeds the rate at which Li can be transported to the interface within the anode
insights.locator: Voids can form at the lithium/ceramic

insights.claim: Voiding during discharge also seeds dendrite failure: lost contact area raises local current density on the next charge, so dendrites initiate at lower charging currents, leading to short circuit.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Fixing discharge voiding has knock-on benefits for charge-side reliability and cycle life.
insights.locator: Voids can form at the lithium/ceramic

insights.claim: Voiding in lithium-metal solid-state cells can be alleviated by stack pressures above about 10 MPa so lithium creep keeps up with discharge, but practical solid-state batteries will very likely need to operate at 2 MPa or less, so high pressure is not a viable fix.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Pack-level pressure hardware is a cost/weight burden; solutions that work at <=2 MPa are commercially decisive.
insights.quote: practical solid-state batteries are very unlikely to operate at such high stack pressures; typically, ≤2 MPa will be required
insights.locator: Voiding can be alleviated to some extent

insights.claim: Existing approaches to discharge voiding in solid-state batteries rely on new materials: lithium alloys for faster Li transport, interlayers between lithium and the ceramic electrolyte, and 3D mixed ionic-electronic conductor architectures in the anode.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Maps the competing technical routes; contouring competes as a materials-free, geometry-only option.
insights.locator: Voiding can be alleviated to some extent

themes.theme: Interface contouring: a materials-free geometric fix and its design rules

insights.claim: Contouring the lithium/ceramic electrolyte interface with a periodic 3D topography requires no new materials, alloys or interlayers and enlarges interfacial area to cut local current density, though it also creates current hot spots where voiding is most likely to begin.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: A process-only change could be easier to adopt in existing sulfide-electrolyte cell lines than new chemistries.

insights.claim: Among frustum-of-square-pyramid, egg-box and square-pyramid topographies, the sinusoidal egg-box shape gives the highest critical current of stripping because it avoids sharp corners where local current spikes.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Specific geometry choice matters; sharp-cornered patterns underperform.
insights.locator: Optimizing the contour geometry

insights.claim: For egg-box-contoured Li/Li6PS5Cl interfaces, the highest critical stripping current comes from low peaks placed close together, because lower trough current density, low trough pressure aiding lithium creep, and shorter diffusion paths for Li flux all coincide only in that regime.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete design target (fine, shallow features) for manufacturers pursuing patterned electrolytes.

insights.claim: Contoured Li/solid electrolyte interfaces enhance Li flux toward the troughs in a way analogous to how microelectrodes enhance mass transport in liquid electrochemistry, but taller peaks lengthen the diffusion path, which dominates over the curvature benefit.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Mechanistic basis suggests further gains from finer patterning if manufacturing resolution allows.
insights.quote: Higher curvature enhances the local flux, but increasing peak height lengthens the diffusion path, which turns out to be the more important effect.

insights.claim: Contour features finer than tested could not be explored due to 3D-printing resolution limits, and at very small scales the benefit is expected to be swamped by stochastic electrolyte surface defects, so the electrolyte defect population may set the lower bound on useful contour size.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Signals a ceiling on the approach and makes electrolyte surface quality a co-requirement.
insights.quote: The lower limit of the contoured regime may therefore ultimately be set by the electrolyte surface defect population.

insights.claim: An egg-box contour with 5 µm peak height and 30 µm peak separation was selected as the optimized geometry for Li/Li6PS5Cl solid-state cells.

themes.theme: Full-cell results, energy-density trade-off and path to commercialization

insights.claim: An egg-box contour of 5 µm height and 30 µm separation reduces the theoretical volumetric energy density of a lithium-metal solid-state battery by only about 5% versus a flat interface, while larger contours (25 µm/150 µm) markedly compromise energy density.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: A ~5% energy-density cost for ~10x discharge rate is a favorable trade for EV applications.
insights.quote: reduces the volumetric energy density by only 5% while substantially increasing the discharge rate capabilities of the cell
insights.locator: Implications of contouring on energy density

insights.claim: A full cell with an ~80 µm contoured Li6PS5Cl electrolyte and a ~120 µm LiNi0.83Mn0.06Co0.11O2 composite cathode cycled stably at 6 mA cm−2 discharge and 0.5 mA cm−2 charge (4 mAh cm−2) at 2 MPa and 60 °C, while the non-contoured counterpart failed during the second charge.

insights.so_what: Demonstrates the benefit carries into full cells with NMC cathodes at commercially relevant areal capacity.

insights.claim: Combining contouring with a Li-rich Ag alloy anode (0.5% Ag) with faster Li diffusivity further improved pulse-stripping stability to 20 cycles, and the approach could extend to other fast-transport alloy anodes.

insights.so_what: Contouring is additive with alloy-anode strategies rather than competing with them.

insights.claim: Contouring improves charging (dendrite) critical currents by at most about 50%, so it must be paired with separate dendrite-mitigation strategies for charging even though it strongly helps discharge.
